title: No interface carries the reporting output after INT-19 and INT-20 are removed
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, rows INT-19 and INT-20; Architecture v5 slides 37 (no data lake) and 44 (job map); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17
description: Version 3 names INT-19 (case, queue, decision and outcome data to the data lake and Power BI, nightly) and INT-20 (decisions and outcomes to COLLINS for model learning, nightly) as the only reporting and model-learning outbound interfaces, both owned by the Workbench and retried in the next window. Architecture v5 has no data lake and DP-17 removes both rows: reporting becomes a read model in rwb-reporting built from events, JOB-13 becomes continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision and JOB-15 becomes an Airflow trigger. No source then names the interface that delivers the rwb-reporting read model to Power BI or to a regulator, or the interface that carries decision records to the model owner for learning, so version 4 removes the two rows and adds no replacement. Without an interface the reporting story has an output nobody receives, and the model-learning need of COLLINS has no path at all.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-19 | Data lake and Power BI | Case, queue, decision and outcome data for reporting | Out | Daily batch | Workbench | Nightly' and 'INT-20 | COLLINS | Decisions and outcomes for model learning | Out | Daily batch to the data lake | Workbench | Nightly'. Architecture v5 slide 37: 'Interface Specifications v3: INT-19/20 (data lake, Power BI) are removed'. Architecture v5 slide 8 notes: 'No data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed)'. Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-13 and JOB-15. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting; none; gap if the story needs lake data'.
proposed: Agree the reporting output path with the reporting owner and the business: either a REST or file interface from rwb-reporting to the bank reporting layer and Power BI, or a second Kafka consumer outside the 19 services, and give it the next free interface ID. Agree separately whether COLLINS model learning is served from the decision records on rwb.decision-record.v1 and by whom.

title: INT-21 reads the group-to-role mapping through v_ace_iam_group, which only rwb-source-data may read
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, row INT-21; Architecture v5 slide 9 note and slide 30 (1) and (6); ADR-010
description: Version 3 holds the group-to-role mapping in iam_group, a new ACE table raised in RWB-ACE-001, and reads it through v_ace_iam_group.entra_group at each sign-in, with the ACE team as the owner. ADR-010 and Architecture v5 slide 9 keep the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data, and Architecture v5 slide 30 (1) puts Recovery roles, scope, masking and DoA in rwb-access as data. Neither source says how the mapping travels from the view that rwb-source-data may read to the rwb-access cache that needs it, so the interface row cannot name a read path that both rules allow.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-21: 'Sign-in and the roles each user holds | In | ACE sign-in; group-to-role mapping read through v_ace_iam_group | ACE team | Sign-in | ... group-to-role mapping held in iam_group (new ACE table) and read through v_ace_iam_group.entra_group'. Architecture v5 slide 9 note: 'only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010)'. Architecture v5 slide 30 (1): 'gateway-bff and rwb-access use ACE's Entra-based sign-in; Recovery roles, scope, masking and DoA stay as data in rwb-access'. Architecture v5 slide 30 (6): 'Shared entities ... come from the ACE database through the views, read only by rwb-source-data'.
proposed: Confirm the path: rwb-source-data reads v_ace_iam_group and publishes the mapping as reference data on its own topic or contract, and rwb-access subscribes and caches it, with the ACE team keeping the table and the view. Record the choice in the access and security design and in the P1 and P4 contract stories.

title: INT-34 (ACE Common) has five consumers and no single owning service
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, row INT-34; Architecture v5 slides 17, 30 and 41; Ownership Map v1, sheet Services
description: INT-34 is one published module interface to ACE Common that covers six capabilities, and Architecture v5 slide 30 gives each capability a different consumer: sign-in and access checks to gateway-bff and rwb-access, audit and PII logging to all 19 services, the shared case view to rwb-case, the restructure calculator to rwb-treatment, the notification path to rwb-comms and the shared entities to rwb-source-data. Version 3 gives the row a single owner, the ACE team, and a single owner of the fix, also the ACE team. The realignment needs one Recovery-side owner per interface and no source states which service holds the contract for the whole of INT-34.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-34: 'ACE common module | Shared case view, entities, restructure calculator, notification path | Both | Published module interface | ACE team | Call or application event | As published by the common module | Per request | Per call | Return the error to the calling module | As the caller decides | ACE team | Module interface | DL14'. Architecture v5 slide 30 rows 1 to 6 with the consumer named per capability. Architecture v5 slide 17: 'DB writes schema rwb_integration: interface config, file runs, outbound items, ACE integration paths'. Ownership Map v1, sheet Services: P2 rwb-integration, Integration.
proposed: Agree whether INT-34 stays one interface with rwb-integration as the contract owner and a per-capability client in each consuming service, or splits into one interface row per capability with the consuming service as owner. If it splits, add the new rows in the next version and give each one the capability name of Architecture v5 slide 30.

title: INT-14 (WIN registered mail) has three different owners in the sources
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Service Catalog v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, row INT-14; Architecture v5 slides 8, 17 and 30 (5); Ownership Map v1, sheet Rulings, row JOB-10; Service Catalog v1 section 6.6
description: Version 3 makes the single Workbench the owner of INT-14 and the owner of the fix an owning team plus the platform administrator. Architecture v5 slide 17 puts the WIN outbound file in rwb-integration, which builds the file and owns the file run, while slide 30 (5) says WIN letters go as a file via rwb-integration and the notice itself is rwb-comms. The Ownership Map ruling for JOB-10 records rwb-comms as the owner of the notice and of the 16:00 window, with rwb-integration performing deliverFile, and the Service Catalog v1 gives the P6 file contract as 'WIN letters handed to rwb-integration (INT-14)'. Two services therefore share the interface and no source names one owner.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-14: 'WIN | Demand, recall and sale notices for registered mail | Out | Batch: outbound file through the integration adapters | Workbench | Notice approved and generated | ... | Owning team, platform administrator'. Architecture v5 slide 17: 'FILE WIN (registered mail): daily outbound file (INT-14)'. Architecture v5 slide 30 (5) note: 'WIN letters go as a file via rwb-integration'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings JOB-10: 'rwb-comms (P6) owns the notice and the 16:00 window, and rwb-integration (P2) performs deliverFile as a step'. Service Catalog v1, P6 contract by call type, File row.
proposed: Confirm rwb-comms as the owner of INT-14 (the notice, the addressee and the content of the file) and rwb-integration as the executor of the transfer, and write the split into the P6 and P2 contract stories so that the retry and the acknowledgement have one owner.

title: INT-25 (debt-buyer data tape) is owned by the Workbench in v3 and by two services in the target
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Service Catalog v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, row INT-25; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 30; Service Catalog v1 section 6.15
description: Version 3 makes the single Workbench the owner of INT-25, the data tape for an awarded lot, and the owner of the fix an owning team plus the platform administrator. Architecture v5 slide 17 puts the debt-buyer encrypted files in rwb-integration, which builds the file and the manifest, while the Service Catalog v1 gives the S6 file contract as 'Buyer file per lot through rwb-integration (INT-25)'. The lot, the accounts and the personal data allowed by the sale terms are rwb-debtsale data. No source names one owner of the interface.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-25: 'Debt buyers | Debt sale data tape for an awarded lot | Out | Batch: outbound file through the integration adapters | Workbench | Lot awarded | BorrCode, OS By Acct, SellingPriceByAcct ... | Owning team, platform administrator'. Architecture v5 slide 17: 'Debt buyers: per lot, encrypted (INT-25)'. Service Catalog v1, S6 contract by call type, File row: 'Buyer file per lot through rwb-integration (INT-25)'.
proposed: Confirm rwb-debtsale as the owner of INT-25 (the lot, the account set and the content of the tape) and rwb-integration as the executor of the encrypted transfer, and write the split into the S6 and P2 contract stories.

title: INT-24 is screen-based through the external gateway in v3 and gateway-based around rwb-partner in Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, row INT-24; Architecture v5 slide 8 and its note
description: Version 3 describes INT-24 as Workbench screens through the external gateway, with the single Workbench as owner, the partner and agency manager as owner of the fix and OpenAPI 3.1 as the standard. Architecture v5 slide 8 says partners use the partner gateway with FAPI 2.0 that fronts rwb-partner, and Architecture v5 slide 30 lists no partner row among the ACE Common capabilities. The integration style therefore differs between the sources, and neither states whether an instruction to a partner is issued as a REST call carrying documents or as a file over the partner gateway.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-24: 'Partner portal | Instructions to partners and the results they report | Both | Workbench screens through the external gateway | Workbench | Instruction sent or result entered | ... | Show the error to the partner user and keep the entry | The user submits again | Partner and agency manager | OpenAPI 3.1 | DL03'. Architecture v5 slide 8 note: 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'. Architecture v5 slide 8 diagram: 'Partner gateway FAPI 2.0 -> S9'.
proposed: Confirm that INT-24 is the partner gateway interface of rwb-partner (FAPI 2.0, REST, no screen owned by the Workbench beyond the partner portal), that instructions and results travel on it, and whether a file variant exists for firms that cannot use the API.

title: No PII topic, schema or sender library is named for INT-22, the audit and PII path
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, row INT-22; Architecture v5 slides 23 and 30 (2)
description: Version 3 gives INT-22 the direction Out, the owner the ACE team, the standard AsyncAPI 3.0 and the payload 'Who, what, when, which record, which fields', sent as events happen, with the ACE logging service setting the retry. Architecture v5 slide 30 (2) says every service sends audit and personal-data access logs through ACE's PII Kafka path to the SOC, and slide 23 says Recovery gets its own business-event topics, separate from ACE's PII logging topics. Neither source names the PII topic, its message schema, the library that writes it or the alert when the SOC path is down, so no service can implement the interface from the documents.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-22: 'PII Kafka, audit and SOC logs | Personal data access, audit and security events | Out | ACE logging | ACE team | Each event | Who, what, when, which record, which fields | As they happen | ... | As the ACE logging service | As the ACE logging service | ACE team | AsyncAPI 3.0 | None'. Architecture v5 slide 30 (2): 'every service sends audit and personal-data access logs through ACE's PII Kafka path to the SOC'. Architecture v5 slide 23: 'Recovery gets its own business-event topics and access rules, separate from ACE's PII logging topics'.
proposed: Obtain the PII topic name, the message schema, the client library and the delivery guarantee from the ACE team and record them against INT-22, and state in the observability story that the library is used and not written by each service.

title: Field mapping and Key cite Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7 while v8 is the latest in the set
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Field mapping, row 2 description and sheet Key, row 'LDM field'
description: The Field mapping description says the mappings are per the LDM v7 ACE mapping sheet and the Key row says the field ID is the one of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7. The latest document in the set is v8, and this run produces the next version of the LDM. The field IDs of the format DF-XXX-nnn do not change, so only the citation of the version is out of date; nothing in the mapping changes.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 sheet Field mapping row 2: 'per the LDM v7 ACE mapping sheet'. Sheet Key row 'LDM field': 'The field ID in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7'. _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md is present in the run material.
proposed: Repoint the two citations at the next LDM version when it is issued, and check that every DF-* field ID of the mapping still exists in it; no row of the mapping is expected to change.

title: INT-35 and INT-36 name no consuming service
source: Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Interface Specifications v3, sheet Interfaces, rows INT-35 and INT-36; Architecture v5 slides 18 and 30 (4); Ownership Map v1, sheet Rulings, row signature_request
description: INT-35 carries the NLEADS credit approval result for a restructure plan and INT-36 the EasyApp e-signature reference and status for a restructure agreement; both are new ACE inbound interfaces raised in RWB-ACE-001, read through a v_ace_* view, with the ACE team as owner and owner of the fix. The business consumer is not named on either row: the restructure plan belongs to the treatment stage and the signature request is a P5 rwb-document table under the Ownership Map ruling. Version 4 records the read path as rwb-source-data under ADR-010, and the consuming service is left to the stage story.
evidence: Interface Specifications v3 rows INT-35 and INT-36 with payload nleads_ref, credit_result, credit_result_reason, decided_at and external_ref, owner ACE team. Architecture v5 slide 18 (treatment stage, restructure) and slide 30 (4) (restructure calculator called by rwb-treatment). Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings signature_request: 'signature_request is P5 rwb-document (Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41, signatures); P6 orchestrates the request through P5's contract'.
proposed: Confirm rwb-treatment as the consumer of INT-35 and rwb-document as the consumer of INT-36, reading both through the rwb-source-data contract, and name the consumer in the next version of the row.
